chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Rafa'ah who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding a man who struck a man, so some of his breathing was deficient. With what thing would that be known?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'By the hours.' I said, 'And how by the hours?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'For indeed, the breath rises at dawn, and it is in the right side of the nose. So when an hour passes, it moves to the left side. So you look at the difference between your breathing and his breathing. Then it is reckoned, so he is taken by that calculation from it.'

key_terms.السَّاعَات: The hours (referring to the hourly cycle of nostril dominance)

ai.seo_question: How is compensation calculated for an injury that impairs breathing according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the physiological basis for calculating compensation (diyah) for injuries affecting respiration, specifically noting the alternating nature of nasal breathing. The Imam explains that breath shifts between nostrils in hourly cycles, allowing for precise quantification of impairment by comparing the victim's breathing rhythm to that of a healthy person. This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking medical observation with legal jurisprudence to ensure equitable compensation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Rafa’at who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding a man who struck a man, so some of his breathing was deficient. With what thing would that be known?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By the timing’. I said, ‘And how by the timing?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘At the emergence of dawn, he is breathing, and it is from the right nostril. So when an hour goes by, he (comes to be) breathing by the left nostril. So you would look at what (difference) there is between your breathing, and his breathing. Then it would be reckoned, so he would be taking by that counting from it’.
